messages:
liam: Heads up — staging p95 token latency up ~18% after last runtime deploy (commit d4c3f7a). Mostly on long-context jobs (8k tokens) with our default batching.

maya: saw this too. p50 is fine, but p95 jumps. Reproduced locally against staging image with synthetic trace. Seems correlated with attention kernel path selection.

kat: ran microbench quick comparison between paged-attn and flash variants on A100. Quick notes: paged is lower and tighter tail when KV cache is hot; Flash variants show worse tail on cold KV/cold-prefix cases.

perf-ci: benchmark output pasted below (single-run):
```
bench --model=gpt-mini --seq=8192 --batch=1 --kernel=flash_v2
tokens/s: 2180
p50 token latency: 4.6ms
p95 token latency: 19.8ms
p99 token latency: 32.4ms

bench --kernel=paged_attn
tokens/s: 2350
p50 token latency: 4.2ms
p95 token latency: 11.7ms
p99 token latency: 18.3ms
```

liam: interesting — flash_v2 gives similar median but much worse tail. On production traces the p95 spikes line up with prefix refreshes (KV cache misses) and when a batch mixes requests with different KV states.

dena: I started a git bisect on the runtime repo. Bad at d4c3f7a, good at 0a1b2c3 (two weeks ago). d4c3f7a changed kernel selection ordering and touched batching heuristics.

kat: diff summary: selectKernel() used to prefer paged for seq>=4096 then flash fallback; new change flipped preference for better single-stream throughput in a number of cases, but didn't account for mixed-KV batches. Pseudocode: 
```
- if (seq_len >= 4096) choose paged
+ if (batch_wide_avg_seq < 4096 || mixed_kv_state) choose flash_v2
```

maya: that matches the behavior — when batches include both warmed and cold KV entries, flash path triggers heavy per-request memory ops causing tail latency. Paged path keeps KV streaming and reduces contention.

liam: can we either (a) bias kernel selection to paged when batch has any cold-KV, or (b) tweak batching so we don't mix KV states? Which is lower risk?

dena: lower risk is adjusting selection bias in runtime for canary. I'll prepare a patch to prefer paged when >1% of batch items have KV_miss or when kv_miss_ratio > 0.1.

kat: I can land a quick revert of the ordering for canary if we want an immediate rollback. Will test canary with 1000 real requests.

perf-ci: small flamegraph attached (link) — shows heavy time in memcpy + kernel-launch stalls for flash_v2 on cold-KV.

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled by kat for next 10m window.

maya: action items: dena will open runtime PR with selection bias, kat will deploy canary rollback if needed, i'll run production-like eval against the canary and post numbers.

liam: thanks — please ping #oncall if we see >10% user-facing errors. :thumbsup:

kat: quick note — also seeing a small regressive delta in batching heuristic where batch-slicing constrains max_tokens_per_batch; I'll include that in the PR (avoid shrinking batches when seq variance high).
